Johnson, M.R., Crosland, B.M., McEwen, J.D., Hager, D.B., Armitage, J.R., Karimi-Golpayegani, M., Picard, D.J. (2016). Estimating fugitive methane emissions from oil sands mining using extractive core samples. Atmospheric Environment 144, 111-123. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.atmosenv.2016.08.073

Loaded (main): mine-face/ore fugitive CH4 and CO2 emission factors for an Alberta oil sands surface mine from core-sample residual gas (per kg bitumen, per kg disturbed material, and Table 2 kgCO2e/m3-bitumen at GWP 25 and 36), plus a derived kg CH4/m3-bitumen (779 mg/kg x 990 kg/m3) and three reprinted literature estimates (GHGenius 480 L/t bitumen, WorleyParsons 2009, Bergerson 2012) as separate processes. All are emissions-process under archetype mine_open-pit-oil-sands, but cover the fugitive component only, not combustion or the whole plant. 95% CI min/max derived from printed +/- bounds. Other-values: AER ST39 Alberta 2015 activity (mined material, grade, bitumen, disturbed material), Alberta fugitive CH4 totals, bitumen density and HHV, Syncrude flux-chamber 2274 kgCH4/km2/day, NIR and Brandt aggregate factors. TRAP: Table 1 fugitive CO2 [Mt] row reprints the CH4 kt numbers (37...58); the text gives ~0.2 Mt. Not loaded: per-sample data (supplementary tables S.1/S.2, not in the PDF), figures. Page numbers are printed journal pages (111-123).
